pages.text: Deuterium and tritium fuse into helium-4 and a neutron, giving $(thing)17.6 MeV$(). They must be hot (10-20 keV, over a hundred million kelvin), dense, and held long enough: Lawson's $(thing)nTτ ≥ 3×10²¹ keV·s/m³$().

The $(item)Tokamak$() holds the plasma in a torus of twisted field: twelve toroidal field coils, a central solenoid, a vacuum vessel. Set the density, temperature and field; confinement grows with the field squared. Keep β - plasma pressure against magnetic - under 5%, or the plasma disrupts. The coils are superconducting: below 20 K, and below 12.5 T.
A $(item)Fusion Blanket Tile$() of lithium-6 breeds more tritium than the reaction burns. Deuterium alone burns too - but needs five times the triple product.
